key_concepts: Electric current is the number of electric charges passing through a conductor cross-secti
Conventional current flows from the positive to the negative battery terminal
Current is measured in amperes using an ammeter
Voltage is the electrical pressure or force that pushes charges through a circuit
Batteries transform chemical energy into electrical energy and contain an electrolyte
Voltage is measured in volts using a voltmeter connected across the load
Resistance is the hindrance to the flow of electric charges
Higher voltage produces higher current, while higher resistance produces lower current
Simple circuits include a source, load, switch, wires, and measuring devices
